lead.headline: Nasdaq Slides Into Correction as Nvidia's Board Shuts the Door on Huang Hours Before Results
lead.deck: Wall Street fell for a third straight session, with the Nasdaq down 2.5% and nearly 11% below its October peak, while Indian shares bucked the trend on heavy foreign buying.
body: The AI sell-off deepened on Monday. The S&P 500 fell 1.92% to 7,416.59, the Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.49% to 24,509.76 and the Dow lost 739 points, or 1.41%. It was a third consecutive losing day for all three, and the Nasdaq now sits about 10.9% below its 6 October high, meeting the usual definition of a correction. The VIX volatility gauge jumped as high as 24 during the afternoon.

Nvidia, down about 4%, led the decline after reports that its board is not considering reinstating Jensen Huang, who resigned as chief executive last week, despite a supporters' petition that now claims more than 180,000 signatures. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent has urged the board to hire from outside and says he wants answers within ten days on whether the company's chips reached China via Singapore and other Asian markets. President Trump said he would not object to Huang's return.

There was little relief from the data. The New York Fed's Empire State manufacturing index fell to 7.8 in November, far below forecasts, and Fed Chair Kevin Warsh cautioned that AI might disappoint. Treasuries rallied modestly, with the 10-year yield easing to roughly 5.12% from 5.15%. Asian chip stocks extended losses on Tuesday morning, with the Kospi slipping below 5,000.

India was the exception. The Sensex rose 0.63% and the Nifty 0.58% as foreign investors bought about ₹5,737 crore of shares and rotated away from AI-heavy markets, even as wholesale inflation climbed to 12.29% in October, the highest in the current series. Nvidia reports after the US close tonight (early Wednesday in India), and Anthropic is due to price its IPO on Wednesday.

top: The Nasdaq fell 2.5% into correction territory as Nvidia's board signalled it will not bring back Jensen Huang ahead of Tuesday's results.
India's wholesale inflation rose to 12.29% in October on surging fuel and power prices, the highest in the current WPI series.
Québecor has made an unsolicited, roughly C$31 billion proposal for Telus, sending its shares up 12%.
Aon completed its $17 billion purchase of USI, and Canadian Natural agreed to buy Advantage Energy in a $2.53 billion deal.
Activist Land & Buildings is pressing Invitation Homes to sell houses and return $2 billion a year to shareholders.

items.fig: Nasdaq −10.9% from 6 Oct high · VIX intraday 24.05
items.headline: Wall Street Extends Losing Streak to Three Days
items.body: Tech led a broad sell-off as investors cut AI exposure before Nvidia's earnings. A sharp miss on the Empire State factory survey added to the gloom.

items.headline: Chip Selling Hits Tokyo and Seoul; Europe Holds Up Better
items.body: The Nikkei closed below 60,000 and the Kospi tumbled on Monday, and both opened lower again on Tuesday. European shares eased only slightly from Friday's record, helped by softer oil and bond yields.

items.headline: Indian Wholesale Inflation Hits Series High
items.body: Fuel and power prices drove the third straight monthly rise, though the reading was slightly below market estimates and ICRA thinks it may mark the peak. Retail inflation is already above the RBI's 6% ceiling.

items.headline: Bonds Catch a Bid as Oil and Gold Ease
items.body: Treasury yields slipped a few basis points as stocks fell. Brent dropped about 1%, which helped the rupee firm to around 93.92 per dollar.

items.headline: Nvidia Slides Again Before First Results Without Huang
items.body: Analysts say the key question tonight is whether management keeps or withdraws its guidance for roughly 70% sales growth next fiscal year, given export-control uncertainty.

items.headline: Tata Motors PV Drags as Consumer Names Lift the Nifty
items.body: Tata Motors' passenger-vehicle arm was the worst Nifty stock after its quarterly results, while FMCG and hospital stocks led gains. Kaynes Technology sank 13% after its quarterly profit fell about 62%.

items.headline: Drug Regulators and Trials Swing Biotech Shares
items.body: Summit Therapeutics fell after the FDA declined to approve its lung cancer drug in its current form, while CG Oncology rallied on a successful late-stage bladder cancer trial.

items.headline: Tyson Rises; Red Cat Pulls Its Forecast
items.body: Tyson Foods climbed on mixed quarterly results, while drone maker Red Cat slumped in late trading after withdrawing its 2026 revenue target.

items.headline: Québecor Makes Unsolicited Play for Telus
items.body: Telus confirmed the non-binding approach and said it undervalues the company and would leave holders in a more leveraged group. Ottawa says competition and telecom regulators would review any deal.

items.headline: Aon Closes Its Purchase of Broker USI
items.body: The deal adds a large US middle-market brokerage that will keep its brand as an Aon company. Aon expects about $395 million of annual cost and revenue synergies.

items.headline: Canadian Natural to Buy Advantage Energy
items.body: The deal adds about 79,000 barrels of oil equivalent a day of output in Alberta and is targeted to close in the first quarter of 2027.

items.headline: Hormel Completes Brakebush Acquisition
items.body: The food company closed its purchase of the chicken processor, according to a regulatory filing.

items.fig: Target ≥$2bn a year in returns · NAV est. ≈$45/share
items.headline: Land & Buildings Takes Aim at Invitation Homes
items.body: Jonathan Litt's fund argues the single-family landlord's shares trade far below the value of its houses and wants it to sell homes and scale back acquisitions. It has hinted at a 2027 proxy fight.

items.headline: Third-Quarter Holdings Filings Land
items.body: Big managers disclosed 30 September positions, giving a view of AI exposure before the November sell-off. Early reports say Bridgewater added Nvidia and Broadcom and trimmed Alphabet and Amazon.

items.headline: Einhorn's DME Capital Builds an MGM Stake
items.body: David Einhorn's fund opened a new position in MGM Resorts during the third quarter, according to its latest filing.

items.headline: Anthropic IPO Heads to Pricing on Strong Demand
items.body: Reports say orders cover the shares on offer several times over, and existing backers will get priority in allocations. Trading is set to begin on Thursday.

items.fig: FII buy ≈₹5,737 cr · DII sell ≈₹2,254 cr
items.headline: Foreign Money Returns to Indian Equities
items.body: Overseas funds were heavy buyers on Monday as investors looked for markets less exposed to the AI trade. Midcaps and smallcaps still lagged.

items.headline: Razorpay and MakeMyTrip India Line Up Listings
items.body: Both have SEBI clearance, keeping the IPO pipeline busy even as weekly startup funding slumped 90% to $25.2 million last week.

items.headline: Inox Wind CEO Resigns After Weak Quarter
items.body: The wind-turbine maker's shares fell after it reported weaker September-quarter earnings and announced its chief executive's exit.
